title: Specs for a new HMD Android phone leak
description: According to a reliable source of HMD-related leaks and rumors, the company is working on yet another lower-end Android phone to join its portfolio. It's currently unclear what this handset will be called, but it is allegedly codenamed "Darkhawk". That's probably a codename way too cool for the specs of this device. It will reportedly have a flat screen with a 120Hz refresh rate, 8GB of RAM, and a 6,000 mAh battery with support for 33W wired charging. title: Huawei Mate 90 Pro Max debuts with a 1-inch modular camera, 12,000-nit display and 6,800mAh battery
description: Huawei has unveiled its latest Mate 90 series phones in China, with the Mate 90 Pro Max sitting at the top. The phone offers a large 6.9-inch display, a triple-rear camera setup, and supports a unique 1-inch module camera system. The triple-rear camera setup on the Mate 90 Pro Max comes with a 50MP main camera that uses a 1/1.28-inch RYYB sensor with OIS and a continuous variable f/1.4 to f/4.0 aperture. title: vivo Y600 5G is coming and it will be familiar
description: The vivo Y600 5G has just been listed in the Google Play Console, with the model number V2626. Its model number reveals the fact that it will be the same device as the Malaysian V80 Lite 5G as well as the Indian S2 FE, which is due to be launched on October 6. The Google Play Console listing reveals that the vivo Y600 5G has 1260x2800 resolution, the MediaTek MT6858 chipset, 6GB of RAM, and Android 16 on board, rather disappointingly. title: Here's how the Galaxy S27 series prices will go up according to a new rumor
description: According to a new rumor from Samsung's home country of South Korea, the Galaxy S27 series devices will be at least KRW 130,000 (about $95) more expensive than their predecessors in the country - but that rate of increase will only apply to the base model. The more expensive storage tiers will get a bigger jump compared to what we've seen for the Galaxy S26 devices. So, for example, the Galaxy S26 Ultra started at $1,299 when it launched. title: vivo X Fold6 finally goes global
description: Exactly three months after being released in China, the vivo X Fold6 has now been announced for global markets, just like a rumor predicted a few days ago. The X Fold6 has an 8.02-inch foldable LTPO AMOLED screen with 2312x2504 resolution, 120Hz refresh rate, and 5,000-nit peak brightness, and a 6.51-inch LTPO AMOLED cover screen with 1120x2528 resolution, 120Hz refresh rate, and 5,000-nit peak brightness. title: Galaxy S27 Ultra said to be heavier than Galaxy S26 Ultra
description: There have been plenty of leaks and rumors surrounding Samsung’s upcoming flagship, the Galaxy S27 Ultra, which is expected to launch early next year. A new rumor has now revealed the phone’s alleged dimensions. While leaked CAD renders of the Galaxy S27 Ultra suggested that the phone would measure 7.97mm in thickness, a new rumor from tipster Ice Universe has now corroborated the figure. title: This is when Apple is rumored to be launching the HomePad
description: Apple's very long-rumored "HomePod with a screen", sometimes referred to as the HomePad, is now said to be finally launching on October 13, according to a new report from Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. This "smart-home hub code-named J490" is allegedly "at the center" of the company's strategy for the smart home. At the same time, Apple will also be launching an updated HomePod mini, as well as a new Apple TV 4K box. title: AT&T is buying $3 billion worth of fibre optic cables from Corning
description: Today, AT&T has signed a new multi-year deal with Corning to purchase fibre optic cables. The deal is valued at more than $3 billion, and will help AT&T reach its stated goal of connecting 60 million homes and businesses with fibre optic cables by 2030. The carrier has already reached 30 million locations, so half of that, in June this year, six months ahead of its initial schedule. title: Samsung Galaxy A18 4G review
Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra in for review
description: The line between tablets and laptops has been increasingly more blurred for the past few years. That's especially true for devices like the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra - a top-of-the-line slate with a huge AMOLED display and a thin profile. It goes the other way as well; laptops nowadays get the same mobile-based chipsets and tablet-like battery life and fluidity. Perhaps the two categories were always destined to meet in the middle. title: Amazon unveils faster Fire TV Stick 4K (2026) and a new Fire TV Remote
description: Amazon just unveiled a slimmer and faster Fire TV Stick 4K (2026) and a new Fire TV Remote. The stick is 20%-40% faster than similarly priced 4K sticks from other brands, says Amazon. The pricing is $60, by the way, but you can have it for half that – see below. The new Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K (2026) is powered by a quad-core 1.7GHz processor with 8GB of internal storage. It supports Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.3 and LE. It can decode up to 4K video at 60fps with the H.264, H.265, VP9 and AV1 codecs. It also supports several HDR formats: HDR10, HDR10+ and HLG. title: More images of the Samsung Galaxy Buds On surface, they show off the clip-on design
description: We first heard of the Galaxy Able buds back when the Galaxy Watch9 and Watch Ultra2 leaks were happening. The watches became official, the buds still are not. Since then we’ve learned that these will become Samsung’s first clip-on style buds and will actually be called the Samsung Galaxy Buds On. Here are a few more details, plus a couple of images. Clip-on buds don’t go into your ear canal like regular buds. Instead, they rely on their clip design to stay on your ears – this can be much more comfortable for long periods. The Galaxy Buds On will reportedly use open-ear air conduction....

title: CEO John Ternus wants Apple to be leaner, more experimental and to launch products faster
description: New CEO John Ternus used to be Apple’s SVP of Hardware Engineering, while Tim Cook was a sales guy. We are now starting to see how Ternus’ leadership will be different from Cook’s – Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Ternus wants to create a “leaner organization” that is focused on engineering. “Leaner” means that there will be some downsizing – apparently, Ternus wants to reduce the number of middle management positions to give engineers a more direct connection to the senior executives. title: Honor 700 Pro with its rear screen to be joined by three other interesting phones this year
description: Earlier this month word got out that Honor's upcoming 700 Pro will have a rear screen just like Xiaomi's 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max (and the 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max before that). Today, the prolific leaker who goes by Digital Chat Station on Weibo has shared some more details about it and Honor's other planned releases for the end of this year. The Honor 700 Pro's rear screen is once again 'confirmed' (as much as a rumor can confirm anything), as is its 200MP main camera, which we've heard about before too. title: AirPods 5 are Apple’s most repairable earbuds ever
description: Wireless earbuds are notoriously difficult to repair and outside of distinct offerings like the Fairphone Fairbuds, there’s virtually no way to repair damaged components. Well, it turns out that Apple has taken a slightly more repair-friendly approach with its latest AirPods 5. The latest teardown from iFixit reveals that Apple is back to using pronged batteries, which are much easier to replace than the glued-in ones on previous iterations. While this is a small win for consumers, the whole process is still very tedious. You’ll need something to clamp the AirPods to and then somehow...

title: The new Samsung SmartTag3 supports iOS, it's also smaller and its battery lasts longer
description: The Samsung SmartTag2 is three years old now and was due for an upgrade. This is the first generation that is cross-platform – it works with both Android and iOS devices. It’s also smaller and lighter, though that came at a cost. New wireless tech allowed Samsung to improve detection range and to extend battery life. The Samsung SmartTag3 can now be used by iPhone owners – this makes it easier if you have Android and iOS devices in your family or if a friend or family member wants to borrow, say, a suitcase with a tag attached. title: Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Galaxy Tab S12+ debut
description: Samsung has unveiled its latest flagship Android tablets, the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Galaxy Tab S12+. The tablets will go on sale in select markets starting October 7. The new Galaxy Tab S12 series tablets share several specifications, although the Ultra model gets a larger display, more RAM and storage, a bigger battery, and a couple of other upgrades over the Plus model. Both the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra and Galaxy Tab S12+ are powered by the MediaTek Dimensity 9500 chipset and run Android 17-based OneUI 9. title: Oppo F35 series pricing leaked ahead of India launch
description: Ahead of their launch in India next week, the prices of the Oppo F35 and F35 Pro have leaked online. The Oppo F35 series is confirmed to feature a 50MP ultrawide front camera with a 100 degree field-of-view. According to the leak, the Oppo F35 will start at INR 37,999 for the 6GB/128GB variant. The phone is tipped to feature a 6.57 inch AMOLED display, a Dimensity 6360 chipset, and a 50MP primary rear camera paired with a 2MP depth sensor. title: Google Pixel 11a CAD-based renders leak showing more of the same
description: Back in July, purported specs for the upcoming Google Pixel 11a leaked, and today we have some CAD-based renders of the device to look at. The source of these renders also confirms one of the key upgrades that were also mentioned in the aforementioned specs leak, namely that the Pixel 11a will be powered by the Tensor G6 chipset, just like the rest of the Pixel 11 devices. The Pixel 11a is reportedly going to be unveiled next spring, so we're still very far from its release.
